articles.full_text:
United Nations Secretary-General Antonio Guterres has called for urgent action to deal with extreme heat, as the UN weather agency forecasts above-normal temperatures across much of the world over the next three months.
Guterres made the appeal in response to the temperature outlook for August through October released on Friday by the World Meteorological Organization.
At a news conference, the UN chief described the climate crisis as "in overdrive."
He said: "Extreme heat has long been called the silent killer. Yet even that description may understate the crisis."
Guterres warned of rising heat-related deaths across the world. He also noted that extreme heat is widening inequalities and deepening hunger.
He urged countries to introduce heat-health action plans and early warning systems. He also called for governments and employers to adjust working hours and take other steps to protect workers from heat. He said protection from extreme heat must be designed into homes, schools and hospitals.
Guterres also appealed for urgent action to reduce the use of oil and other fossil fuels.
He said that "unless we act -- to protect people and tackle the root cause of the crisis -- it will become deadlier still."
